title: Number of Even and Odd Bits
description: Given a positive integer `n`, let `even` be the number of 1-bits located at even 0-indexed bit positions (0, 2, 4, ...) in the binary representation of `n`, and let `odd` be the number of 1-bits located at odd bit positions (1, 3, 5, ...). Return the two-element integer array `[even, odd]`.
hints: Bit positions 0, 2, 4, ... correspond to the alternating bitmask `0x55555555`, while odd positions 1, 3, 5, ... correspond to `0x2AAAAAAA`.
Mask `n` with each constant and count the remaining set bits using popcount in O(1) time.

examples.explanation: 17 in binary is 10001, with 1-bits at positions 0 and 4 (both even), giving [2, 0].
2 in binary is 10, with a single 1-bit at position 1 (odd), giving [0, 1].
50 in binary is 110010, with 1-bits at positions 1, 4, and 5 (one even, two odd), giving [1, 2].
